full_text_zh:
[P1] 以逸待劳

[P2] 秋天到了，赵国雁门门外，金黄的谷子成熟了。百姓和军士们割的割，捆的捆，装的装，沉甸甸的谷子一车接一车地运进了堡子里。忽然，一名士兵骑着快马飞驰而来，高声呼喊：‘狼烟起了，匈奴离这儿还有一百里！’

[P3] 听到这个消息，地里的人都加快了动作。
"大家把谷子都收进堡子里，不能给匈奴人留下一颗粮。"

[P4] 等到远远能看见匈奴人的战马时，地里已经收得干干净净，人、牛、羊和谷子，连个影子都没有了。上百名匈奴人骑马冲了过来，看着光秃秃的田地，一个匈奴兵怒冲冲地说：“唉，又被他们收光了，咱们抢不到粮食和牛羊了。”

[P5] 领头的匈奴兵望着堡垒上的赵军，唾沫横飞地大喊：“喂，你们赵军看见我们就躲，都是缩头乌龟吗？敢不敢出来打一仗？”
他身后的匈奴兵也跟着喊：“缩头乌龟！胆小鬼！打一仗！打一仗！”
可是，城里的士兵没有一个出来应战，也没有回骂一句。

[P6] 一名年轻的赵国士兵被气得满脸通红，他双手抓起长戈，愤愤地说："这伙儿匈奴兵只有百来人，大家跟我冲出去，杀他个有来无回，看他们还敢嚣张！"另一名士兵赶紧拉住他："将军有令，匈奴人来了，我们只能守城，不能出战。谁敢出去跟匈奴人拼命，就要军法处置！"

[P7] 将军的命令真是怪，但是军令如山，谁敢违抗？士兵们只好任由那群匈奴兵骂了好半天，眼睁睁地看着他们毫发无损地骑马回去了。

“可是，我们来到雁门郡当兵，不就是为了打匈奴人，建功立业吗？为什么不让我们出战呢？”

[P8] 雁门郡内，李牧将军接到消息后，只说了一句："做得好！"
李牧将军镇守雁门郡后，建了许多堡子和烽火台，派出了大批士兵出去打探消息。匈奴人一有风吹草动，士兵马上就会点起狼烟。
士兵们每天练骑马，练射箭，练对战，最厉害的勇士还能得到一百金的奖赏。

[P9] 但是，李将军不让士兵们去打匈奴人，这让大家很疑惑。渐渐地，就有人说李牧将军胆小，不敢跟匈奴人硬碰硬。赵王已经很久没有收到战胜的消息了，他也对李牧感到不满意。就连匈奴人也说李牧怕他们，隔三岔五地骑马到赵军面前来兜圈儿，打呼哨，耀武扬威。

[P10] 于是，赵王召回李牧，换了一个新将军去镇守。新将军上任后，匈奴兵一来就去迎战。可是赵军屡战屡败，屡败屡战。雁门郡外的田地没人敢去耕种，长满了野草，赵国人也不敢赶着牛羊出城放牧了。
没有办法，赵王只好再请李牧出来做守将。李牧说："大王，如果您一定要用我，就要允许我像以前一样做。"
赵王无可奈何地答应了。就这样，李牧将军镇守雁门郡十几年，几乎一场仗也没打过。

[P11] 一直到公元前243年，这一年的冬天，北方飘起了鹅毛大雪。匈奴人在草原上游牧，没有保暖的房屋和衣物，人、马、牛和羊冻死无数。李牧将军听到这个消息，镇定地说："跟匈奴作战的时机到了。"

[P12] 然后，他就开始准备起来：四匹马拉的战车，他挑选出了一千三百辆；骁勇善战的骑兵，他挑选出了一万三千名；百金之赏的勇士，他挑选出了五万名；拉弓善射的箭手，他挑选出了十万名！李牧将军把他们组成方阵，操练起来。

[P13] 到了第二年春天，北方的雪还没有停。匈奴人已经没有食物吃，牛羊也没有牧草吃了。他们只好骑上马，带上刀和弓，到赵国来抢粮食。这时候，李牧已经选定一个山谷，设好埋伏，只等匈奴人自投罗网。

[P14] 李牧将军大开雁门郡，放百姓们到城外的草原上去放牧。饿疯了的匈奴人，看见漫山遍野的牛羊，想也不想就扑了上去。
百姓们丢下牛羊逃回雁门郡，几千名赵国的骑兵也被匈奴人打败了。匈奴首领一见赵军这么弱，立刻带着二十万大军来攻打雁门郡。

[P15] 匈奴人被引到了山谷里。谷口的赵军围过来，就像把他们装进了大口袋。山上的利箭呼呼地射下去，狂奔的战车轰隆隆地冲过去，勇敢的士兵挥刀猛砍过去。这一仗，直杀得天昏地暗，日月失色，匈奴惨败。

[P16] 之后的十几年，匈奴人再也不敢靠近赵国了。李牧十几年来坚守不出，养精蓄锐，等待时机，终于一举消灭了十多万匈奴骑兵。这种在打仗前精心准备，等着敌人从远方疲劳赶来的计策，就叫“以逸待劳”。
full_text_en:
[P1] Wait for the weary with rest

[P2] Autumn had arrived. Outside the Yanmen Pass of the State of Zhao, the golden grain had ripened. The people and soldiers were cutting, bundling, and loading the heavy grain, cart after cart, into the fortress. Suddenly, a soldier rode in on a fast horse, shouting: 'The beacon fire has been lit! The Xiongnu are still a hundred miles away!'

[P3] Hearing this news, everyone in the fields sped up their work.
"Everyone, bring all the grain into the fortress—don't leave a single grain for the Xiongnu!"

[P4] When the Huns' warhorses could be seen from afar, the fields had already been cleared completely—there was not a trace of people, cattle, sheep, or grain. Hundreds of Huns galloped forward, staring at the bare fields. One Hun soldier angrily said, "Ah, they've gathered everything again. We won't be able to steal any food or cattle and sheep."

[P5] The leading Xiongnu soldier, looking up at the Zhao troops on the fortress, spat and shouted: "Hey, you Zhao soldiers, you run away as soon as you see us. Are you all cowards? Dare you come out and fight?"
His fellow Xiongnu soldiers behind him shouted in unison: "Cowards! Cowards! Fight! Fight!"
But not a single soldier from the city came out to fight, nor did they reply with a single insult.

[P6] A young Zhao soldier, furious and red-faced, grabbed his halberd and angrily said: "These匈奴 soldiers are only a hundred or so. Everyone, follow me and charge out! Let's kill them all and make them never dare to be arrogant again!" Another soldier quickly held him back: "The general has ordered: when the Xiongnu come, we can only defend the city and must not fight outside. Anyone who dares to go out and fight the Xiongnu will be punished by military law!"

[P7] The general's order is really strange, but military orders are as firm as a mountain—how dare anyone defy them? The soldiers could only let the group of Xiongnu soldiers curse them for a long time, watching helplessly as they rode away unharmed.

“But we came to Yanmen Commandery to serve as soldiers—wasn’t it precisely to fight the Xiongnu, achieve glory, and build a career? Why won’t they let us go out to battle?”

[P8] Inside Yumen Commandery, General Li Mu, upon receiving the news, simply said: "Well done!"
After General Li Mu took command of Yumen Commandery, he built many forts and beacon towers, and sent out large numbers of soldiers to scout for news. Whenever the Xiongnu showed any sign of movement, the soldiers would immediately light the beacon fires.
The soldiers practiced riding horses, shooting arrows, and combat every day. The most skilled warriors could even receive a reward of one hundred gold pieces.

[P9] But General Li did not allow the soldiers to fight the Xiongnu, which puzzled everyone. Gradually, some people said General Li Mu was cowardly and dared not confront the Xiongnu head-on. King Zhao had not received news of victory for a long time, and he was also dissatisfied with Li Mu. Even the Xiongnu said Li Mu feared them, riding up to the Zhao army's front every now and then, circling around, blowing whistles, and showing off their might.

[P10] Thus, King Zhao recalled Li Mu and replaced him with a new general to defend the frontier. After the new general took office, whenever the Xiongnu troops came, the Zhao army would go out to fight. But the Zhao army lost repeatedly, and fought again and again. The fields outside Yanmen Commandery were no longer cultivated, overgrown with wild grass, and the Zhao people dared not drive their cattle and sheep out of the city to graze.
There was no other way, so King Zhao had to invite Li Mu back to serve as the commander. Li Mu said, "Your Majesty, if you must use me, you must allow me to do things as I did before."
King Zhao reluctantly agreed. In this way, General Li Mu guarded Yanmen Commandery for more than ten years, barely fighting a single battle.

[P11] All the way to 243 BC, that winter, heavy snow fell in the north. The Xiongnu, who herded on the grasslands, had no warm houses or clothes, and countless people, horses, cattle, and sheep froze to death. General Li Mu, upon hearing this news, calmly said: "The time to fight the Xiongnu has come."

[P12] Then, he began to prepare: four-horse chariots, he selected one thousand three hundred; brave and valiant cavalry, he selected thirteen thousand; warriors promised a hundred gold rewards, he selected fifty thousand; archers skilled in shooting, he selected one hundred thousand! General Li Mu formed them into battle formations and began training them.

[P13] By the following spring, the snow in the north had still not stopped. The Xiongnu had no food left, and their cattle and sheep had no grass to eat. They could only mount their horses, take their knives and bows, and go to Zhao to steal grain. At this time, Li Mu had already chosen a valley, set up an ambush, and was waiting for the Xiongnu to walk right into it.

[P14] General Li Mu opened the gates of Yanmen Commandery, allowing the civilians to graze their livestock on the grasslands outside the city. The starving Xiongnu, seeing the mountains and fields full of cattle and sheep, rushed forward without hesitation.
Civilians abandoned their cattle and sheep and fled back to Yanmen Commandery, while thousands of Zhao cavalry were also defeated by the Xiongnu. Seeing the Zhao army so weak, the Xiongnu chieftain immediately led a force of 200,000 troops to attack Yanmen Commandery.

[P15] The Xiongnu were lured into a valley. Zhao troops surrounded the valley entrance, as if stuffing them into a giant bag. Arrows rained down from the hills, war chariots thundered forward, and brave soldiers slashed fiercely with their swords. This battle raged until the sky grew dark and the sun and moon seemed to lose their color—the Xiongnu suffered a crushing defeat.

[P16] For the next dozen years, the Xiongnu dared not come near the State of Zhao. Li Mu, for over a decade, remained on the defensive, conserving strength and waiting for the right moment. He finally annihilated over a hundred thousand Xiongnu cavalry. This strategy—carefully preparing before battle and waiting for the enemy to arrive exhausted from a long journey—is called 'waiting for the weary with ease' (Yi Yi Dai Lao).
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页展示了成语“以逸待劳”的标题，配有一名身穿铠甲、披着红色斗篷、手持长剑的武将形象，表情自信，姿态从容。
[P2] 秋天，赵国雁门关外百姓和士兵正在收割、运输谷物，突然一名骑兵飞驰而来，报告狼烟升起，匈奴大军距离尚有一百里。
[P3] 听到匈奴大军逼近的消息后，田里的百姓和士兵们紧急加快收割和运输谷物，一名士兵大声指挥大家将粮食收进堡垒，以防被敌军抢夺。
[P4] 匈奴大军抵达雁门关外，发现田地已被赵国百姓和士兵抢收一空，一名匈奴士兵愤怒地抱怨无法抢到粮食和牲畜。
[P5] 匈奴大军抵达雁门关外，领头的匈奴兵辱骂赵军胆小如鼠，但城内赵军毫无反应，坚守不出。
[P6] 一名年轻的赵国士兵因匈奴兵逼近而愤怒，欲率众出城迎战，被另一名士兵以将军军令为由阻止，强调必须坚守城池，不可出战。
[P7] 匈奴大军在城外辱骂赵军后悻悻离去，赵军士兵们坚守城池，一名年轻士兵对不战而退感到不解和愤怒，质问为何不能出战。
[P8] 本页描绘了李牧将军在雁门郡内接到情报后的反应，他称赞士兵做得好，并介绍了其治军策略：建立堡子和烽火台、派遣士兵侦察、训练士兵骑射对战，并设立重赏激励勇士。
[P9] 本页描述了李牧将军不主动出击匈奴的策略引发赵国士兵、赵王乃至匈奴人的质疑和不满，匈奴人甚至频繁挑衅赵军以示轻蔑。
[P10] 赵王因新将军屡战屡败而召回李牧，李牧提出需按旧法行事才肯出山，赵王无奈同意，此后李牧镇守雁门郡十几年未主动出战。
[P11] 公元前243年冬天，北方大雪，匈奴人因缺乏保暖设施而冻死无数，李牧将军得知后，认为攻打匈奴的时机已到。
[P12] 李牧将军在得知匈奴因大雪冻死无数后，开始大规模整军备战，挑选精兵强将并组成方阵进行操练，为即将发动的反击做准备。
[P13] 匈奴因大雪导致粮草断绝，被迫南下赵国抢粮；李牧早已在山谷设下埋伏，准备趁机歼灭来犯之敌。
[P14] 李牧将军故意打开雁门郡城门，让百姓放牧，引诱饥饿的匈奴人抢夺牛羊，匈奴人趁机发动大规模进攻，赵军骑兵被击败，百姓仓皇逃回城内。
[P15] 李牧将军设伏于山谷，诱敌深入后，赵军从四面围攻，以弓箭、战车和步兵合力歼灭匈奴，取得大胜。
[P16] 李牧坚守十余年，最终一举歼灭十多万匈奴骑兵，成功运用了“以逸待劳”的战术。
